text: C1a-08 closes pass 8. The empties: all 167 read whole as re-reads of their B4 rulings; 16 placed (class 4, my B1's theme, pass 4's floor; 6 also by gates 1, 28, 29); 151 empty (1.9%) in 18 kinds; saturation by kind: 17 of 18 kinds met by room 352 of 705, one new kind after room 318; four kinds the scheme lacks go to the handback. The arguables: 4,876 read at label level; B1's prediction held at the top (T3-005 | T3-021 first of 922 confused pairs; 13 of 19 predicted pairs in the top 20; five missed). The 20 carried placements kept as found, recorded for the handback. No gate amended; the stopping criterion holds. Guard: 16 moves, none outside the readers' and my B1's placements. validate.py C1: 0 errors, 0 warnings. notes-C1.md has the pass 8 section; the head is rewritten (2,944 words). Next: pass 9, the views, then the form pass.

Close retried: done.sh refused the first attempt because the head named the form-pass id FP-01 in the next comparison, an unresolved link; the phrase now names the ids without the token. Head 2,949 words.

Views after pass 8's close (c1_views_diff.py; _views regenerated 14 Oct 01:40 from assignments_final.jsonl): 10,593 placements against 13,365 on the settled line, 16 more than after pass 7 (10,577), which are the 16 empties placed at pass 8, one theme each; 194 themes placed; T3-140, T3-144 and T3-161 placed nowhere; nine themes in one room each. The rooms-x-third matrix has 705 room rows under a comment line and the header. Nothing in the views asks for a recut; pass 9 goes to the form pass.

Form pass, sweep 1 (form: turn shape, position, length, timing), section 7. Counted with mem.py codes --grep through out/_analysis/c1_form_pass.py (one logged read per pattern, no limit on the count; the helper keeps concepts whose quoted words match, since mem.py also matches the coder's label and note; patterns in c1_form_patterns.json). Whole store: 115,388 concepts in 705 rooms; 9.7% (11,164) are three words or fewer, in 659 rooms; posts 38,641, comments 76,747. Short concepts draw a coded reply by another author in 20.9%, against 35.0% for concepts of 11 words or more. The cheapest act: the one-line reply that joins, assents, reports done or thanks ('I'm in', 'On it', 'Done.', 'Yes', 'Thanks!'): 590 concepts in 337 rooms, median two words, 90.3% under a coded parent item (baseline 73.7%), parents mostly border talk, calls and proposals; cited as a placed theme's support 33.9% (baseline 41.7%); 88 line themes, none above 11.2%. Two turn forms owned by no theme: the edited post (EDIT or UPDATE lines; 1,124 concepts in 418 rooms, 101 line themes, top 10.7%) and talk of sleep, waking and time zones (362 concepts in 219 rooms, 64 line themes, top 13.5%). 'We did it' (800 in 367 rooms) is owned: T3-009 holds 64.1%. Limit: items the coders dropped (no code, no coded descendant) are invisible, so the shortest replies are undercounted and 'no coded reply' is an upper bound on unanswered turns.

Form pass, sweep 2 (register: vocabulary that cuts across subjects). Same helper, 14 patterns plus two recounts. Owned registers: diplomacy (1,102 concepts in 356 rooms; T3-010 and T3-149 hold 58.5%), the medium's craft words (5,790 in 611 rooms; spread, but the words are the canvas itself), pride (T3-009 25.8%), trade (T3-010 26.7%). Polluted counts I recounted: 'gg' matched discord.gg links (game and sport falls from 919 to 291 concepts once links are dropped); 'ranks' and 'squads' are game words in rocketleague and Rainbow6 (military core words: 670 concepts in 260 rooms). The register owned by no theme: the vocabulary of state and war (armies, troops, reinforcements, territory, empire, invasion, annexing, war, battle, enemies, allies, griefers, vandals, traitors): 4,759 concepts in 571 of 705 rooms, under 145 line themes, the largest T3-010 at 14.9% and T3-005 at 13.0%; cited 42.4%, the corpus rate. Kinship words (brothers, family) 634 in 253 rooms, 90 themes, top 9.8%. The plural voice: 'we' words in 28.8% of submission concepts against 16.2% for 'I' words; in replies 'I' leads (11,763 against 9,992). Internet slang and profanity are wide (408 and 505 rooms) and spread, but they are the site's register, not the event's.

Form pass, sweep 3 (what is not said: terms without gloss, roles without introduction, questions nobody answered). The canvas-wide collectives (the void, the blue corner, the green lattice, the rainbow road, the purple) are named in 3,605 concepts in 453 rooms, four of them the collectives' own subs; 118 line themes, top T3-005 17.4%. The void alone: 2,057 concepts in 302 rooms; 128 concepts in 57 rooms put it in a question, and none asks what or who it is (0 concepts match a 'what/who is the void' pattern). The event is named in 11,203 concepts in 684 rooms and explained ('what is r/place', 'how does it work', 'what is this') in 154 concepts in 115 rooms; the cooldown is glossed in 454 concepts in 227 rooms, 342 of them replies, under T3-016 parents most often: the rules are explained to someone who asked. Authority: 'who is in charge / who decides' is asked in 15 concepts in 14 rooms; leaders or offices named in 86 concepts in 61 rooms (game titles dropped). Questions: 13,354 concepts in 674 rooms hold a question mark; 54.5% draw no coded reply by another author; a question in a submission is answered least (37.7%), and 'should we / can we' questions in a submission 36.2% (602 of 943 not). Limit as in sweep 1: an answer the coders dropped is not seen.

Wrote out/form_pass-C1.md (4,006 words): what was searched and at what limits, the three sweeps with their pattern tables, eight form-pass findings under the ids the stage file sets (01 to 08: the one-line reply as the cheapest act; the edited post as a running record; timing the work by who is awake; the vocabulary of state and war as the common speech of canvas work, 571 rooms, 145 line themes; 'we' in posts and 'I' in replies; the canvas-wide collectives named and never glossed; a room's question to itself in a submission answered least; who leads neither asked nor named), each with its communities and lines and quotes grounded with cite.py --grep; the statement that they were never counted and never clustered and that no gate was written for them; and nine things the pass could not reach. The state-and-war finding carries a caution on the named words of T3-010 | T3-149 to the handback; no gate amended.

notes-C1.md: pass 9 section written (opening with the views, the form pass summary with the table of the eight form-pass findings and their communities and lines, the statement that they were never counted, what the form pass could not reach in nine items for stage E1, the stopping criterion holding, the guard at 0 moves in c1_guard_C1a-09.json, doubts, slips, next pass, and the validate.py C1 block: 0 errors, 0 warnings). The nine one-room themes and the three placed nowhere are all rare (checked against scheme_v2.jsonl).

Head rewritten whole for C1a-09: 2,985 words, no id-like tokens (the form-pass ids are named without their tokens). The 19 themes in which scheme_v2 differs from the frozen scheme are now listed by a new read-only script, out/_analysis/c1_scheme_diff_fields.py, which compares the files field by field (discriminators 11, decide_when_both 8, must_show 6, must_not_show 2, tier, floor and gloss 1 each) and gives the same 19 ids the old head named; a whole-record comparison gives 32, because a field held as null in one file and absent in the other counts as a difference there. No .pause file.

C1a-09 closes pass 9. The views after pass 8: 10,593 placements, 16 more than after pass 7. The form pass (section 7), three sweeps over 115,388 concepts on quoted words, counted with mem.py codes --grep through c1_form_pass.py and grounded with cite.py --grep: eight findings in form_pass-C1.md only, never counted and never clustered (the one-line reply as the cheapest act, 590 concepts in 337 rooms; the edited post, 418 rooms; timing by who is awake, 219 rooms; the vocabulary of state and war, 4,759 concepts in 571 rooms under 145 line themes; 'we' in posts and 'I' in replies; the canvas-wide collectives named and never glossed, 453 rooms; submission questions answered least, 37.7%; who leads neither asked nor named, 14 rooms asking). What the pass could not reach, nine items, in form_pass-C1.md and notes-C1.md. No gate amended, no placement moved; the guard counts 0 moves; validate.py C1 0 errors, 0 warnings. Next: the views, then the fourth-order themes (section 8), scheme_v2.md, handback-C1.md and the interview.

Views after pass 9's close (c1_views_diff.py; regenerated 14 Oct 02:09 from the same assignments_final.jsonl hash as after pass 8): unchanged, as pass 9 moved nothing. 10,593 placements against 13,365 on the settled line; 194 themes placed; T3-140, T3-144 and T3-161 placed nowhere; nine rare themes in one room each. out/fourth/ is empty. Pass 10 cuts the fourth-order themes (section 8).

Fourth-order themes (section 8), declared before the first cut. The tier was read whole by family with counts and co-placements (c1_t4_table.py, written to c1_t4_table-C1a-10.txt). The material carries 28 constructs over 195 of 197 third-order themes, because it presents that many distinct mechanisms: a play frame and a host community's boundary around the work; making sense of the canvas and bridging the room's prior frames to it; gathering hands, choosing an emblem, coordinating through the trace, the template, machine workarounds, a backstage, and rare decided order; belief in the room's capability; repair; and between rooms territorial claims, tacit restraint, negotiated order, reciprocity, bodies of rooms, attribution of damage, a repertoire of attack and rivalry; identity in the nation, canvas-born tribes and a moral line on symbols; and at the close the return on being seen, the completion ritual, memory and transition. Partitions tried and set aside: (1) the 21 families as fourth-order themes, rejected because they are topic headings in the material's words and several hold distinct mechanisms (G14 mixes territorial claims, help and host relations; G21 mixes ritual, memory and transition); (2) Puranam, Alexy and Reitzig's four universal problems as the cut, rejected because about 40 themes speak to them and inter-room order, identity and play would be left unpicked; (3) one inter-room order construct for restraint, agreements and help, rejected because tacit restraint, explicit agreement and exchange are different mechanisms and the pair test called T3-010's pairs with T3-149 and T3-151 joints; (4) stigmergy absorbing the emblem themes, rejected because choosing what the mark says is a decision about meaning, and stigmergy is coordination through the trace. Unpicked, listed and not gathered: T3-017 (the sub's ordinary business, the ground boundary work protects) and T3-133 (one hacked sub). Specs in out/_analysis/c1_t4_specs.json; each cut by c1_t4_cut.py, which logs the move and snaps it. 13 borrowed, 14 adapted (all sources recalled, for stage C3), 1 coined; 22 merging, 6 relating.
